column1: # clues.tsv for ft_isdigit -- pedagogic hints only: each line is a QUESTION, never the expected value or the fix.
# Format: <hint><TAB><CASE label><TAB>...   (a line fires if ANY of its cases fails)
Which codes does man ascii give the characters '0' to '9', and is the character '0' the same value as the number 0? What does p.8 say a classification function returns for a character in its class?
Which character sits just before '0' in man ascii, and which just after '9'? Is one of your bounds off by one?

man ascii lists 128 characters, the last one 0x7f: is a code above it in any class of the "C" locale, the one a program runs in until it calls setlocale()? (man 3 toupper, NOTES, says what that locale knows of umlauts.) Does your class have an upper end, and does your function check it?
Which value does <stdio.h> give EOF, and is that value the code of any character?
Which codes in man ascii are not digits? Does one of them get into your class?
